title: Immunogenicity of Two Versus Three Doses of Hepatitis B Vaccine When Administered to Children Aged 2-18 Months: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A 2-dose hepatitis B vaccination schedule is highly immunogenic in children aged ≥1 year, but data for infants are scarce. Our goal was to compare the immunogenicity of 2- and 3-dose hepatitis B vaccination schedules in this population. METHODS: Children in the experimental group were recruited at 2 months of age and randomized to receive a homologous (Infanrix-hexa/Infanrix-hexa) or heterologous (Infanrix-hexa/Twinrix) 2-dose schedule at 2 and 12 months. Children in the control group were recruited at 18 months and had received a homologous 3-dose schedule (Infanrix-hexa/Infanrix-hexa/Infanrix-hexa) at 2, 4, and 18 months. All groups received a challenge dose (Twinrix) 3 years later. RESULTS: One month after the primary series, seroprotection rates (anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL) were high and similar among the 3 groups (heterologous 2-dose, 91.7%; homologous 2-dose, 90.9%; 3-dose, 94.2%). Geometric mean titers (GMTs) were lower in the 2-dose groups than in the 3-dose group. Post-challenge dose, the majority exhibited an anamnestic response, similar across all 3 groups (heterologous 2-dose, 97.2%; homologous 2-dose, 95.5%; 3-dose, 92.7%). GMTs were numerically higher in the heterologous 2-dose group (9380.5 mIU/mL) than in the 3-dose group (6900.6 mIU/mL) (P = .4). The proportion exhibiting local reactions was significantly lower after the heterologous 2-dose schedule than after the homologous 2-dose schedule. CONCLUSIONS: The anamnestic response 3 years after 2-dose (2 and 12 months) and 3-dose (2, 4, and 18 months) hepatitis B vaccination schedules was similar. The heterologous 2-dose schedule was more immunogenic and less reactogenic than the homologous 2-dose schedule.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在比较 2-18 个月儿童中 2 剂和 3 剂乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 方案的免疫原性,因为尽管 2 剂方案对年龄较大的儿童具有高免疫原性,但婴儿数据有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 进行了一项随机临床试验,将两种 2 剂量方案(同源和异源)与 3 剂量方案进行比较,该试验涉及在不同年龄招募并按指定时间间隔接受 疫苗 的儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 儿童在 2 个月和 12 个月时被随机分配接受同源或异源 2 剂方案,或在 2、4 和 18 个月时接受同源 3 剂方案。3 年后,所有组均接受攻击剂量 (Twinrix)。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,2 剂量和 3 剂量方案之间的记忆反应相似,但异源 2 剂量方案比同源 2 剂量方案具有更高的免疫原性和更低的反应原性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,对于 2-18 个月的儿童,2 剂 疫苗接种 方案可能与 3 剂方案一样有效,这可能为婴儿的 疫苗接种 策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的设计和结果因缺乏长期随访和可能存在混杂因素而受到限制,但由于随机临床试验的设置以及免疫原性和反应原性的直接比较,证据是强有力的。

abstract_zh: 背景:2剂乙型肝炎疫苗疫苗接种方案在≥1岁儿童中高度免疫原性,但婴儿期数据缺乏。本研究旨在比较2剂与3剂乙型肝炎疫苗疫苗接种方案在该人群中的免疫原性。方法:实验组儿童于2月龄时招募,随机分配接受同源(Infanrix-hexa/Infanrix-hexa)或异源(Infanrix-hexa/Twinrix)2剂方案,于2月龄和12月龄接种。对照组儿童于18月龄时招募,已接受同源3剂方案(Infanrix-hexa/Infanrix-hexa/Infanrix-hexa),于2月龄、4月龄和18月龄接种。所有组别均于3年后接种加强剂量(Twinrix)。结果:主要免疫程序完成后1个月,3组血清保护率(抗-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL)均较高且相似(异源2剂组91.7%,同源2剂组90.9%,3剂组94.2%)。几何平均滴度(GMT)在2剂组低于3剂组。加强剂量后,大多数受试者均表现出回忆应答,且3组间相似(异源2剂组97.2%,同源2剂组95.5%,3剂组92.7%)。GMT在异源2剂组(9380.5 mIU/mL)数值上高于3剂组(6900.6 mIU/mL)(P = .4)。异源2剂方案的局部反应发生率显著低于同源2剂方案。结论:2剂(2月龄和12月龄)与3剂(2月龄、4月龄和18月龄)乙型肝炎疫苗疫苗接种方案完成3年后的回忆应答相似。异源2剂方案较同源2剂方案更具免疫原性且反应原性更低。

title: Prevalence of Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Cameroon: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a global public health problem, and many regions of Sub-Saharan Africa are disproportionately affected, including Cameroon, where prevalence has previously been shown to be high. This study aimed to provide up-to-date estimates of HBV prevalence in Cameroon. We searched Medline, Global Health, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Africa Index Medicus and the Journal of Health Science and Disease at the University of Yaounde. We included studies reporting HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence in the general population and subpopulations. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to generate pooled estimates of HBsAg prevalence, overall and for population subgroups including those considered at relatively higher-risk and relatively lower-risk of HBV infection. Heterogeneity was assessed using the index of heterogeneity (I 2 ). Quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tool. Out of 1236 records, 92 papers with 100 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Overall prevalence of HBV in Cameroon was 9.98% (95% confidence interval [CI] 9.00-11.02) with high heterogeneity (I 2 = 98.10%). The prevalences for relatively lower-risk and higher-risk populations were8.94% (95% CI 7.84-10.11) and 12.70% (95% CI 10.28-15.32), respectively. In subgroup analyses, we found that sex, geographical area (regions), population risk groups and study design were the main sources of heterogeneity. Overall, HBV prevalence remains high in Cameroon. Our findings suggest an urgent need for health interventions to halt the spread of the disease, with particular attention needed for males and regions with the highest prevalence.

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 我们的研究结果表明,迫切需要采取健康干预措施来阻止疾病的传播,特别需要关注男性和 患病率 最高的地区。所提供的证据并未报告喀麦隆应对乙型肝炎的具体研究重点或政策建议。

title: ALG-020572, an Antisense Oligonucleotide for the Treatment of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection Discontinued for Drug-Induced Liver Injury.
abstract: Current treatment options for chronic HBV infection are suboptimal in that they fail to suppress HBsAg levels. ALG-020572 is an antisense oligonucleotide designed to reduce viral protein synthesis through degradation of HBV mRNA. ALG-020572-401 was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial consisting of two parts. Part 1 (single-ascending doses) evaluated the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of single doses of ALG-020572 or placebo in healthy participants. In Part 2 (multiple dosing), participants with non-cirrhotic HBeAg-negative, virologically suppressed chronic HBV infection were administered up to 7 doses of ALG-020572 to evaluate safety, pharmacokinetics and antiviral activity. In Part 1, 32 participants were randomized to ALG 020572 or placebo. Single doses of ALG-020572 up to 480 mg were well tolerated. The most common treatment-emergent adverse event reported was injection site reaction. ALG-020572 was rapidly absorbed and plasma exposures increased with dose. In Part 2, 8 participants with non-cirrhotic HBeAg-negative virologically suppressed chronic hepatitis B infection were enrolled and received up to 7 doses of ALG-020572. The study was prematurely discontinued after 4 participants experienced significant alanine aminotransferase elevations that were subsequently attributed to drug-induced liver injury. Single doses of ALG-020572 demonstrated a favourable pharmacokinetic and safety profile in healthy participants. The findings highlight the need for caution in developing antisense oligonucleotides for HBV treatment, as they may pose significant safety risks. The study's limitations include its premature discontinuation and small sample size, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 目前针对慢性 HBV 感染的 治疗 方案并不理想,因为它们无法抑制 HBsAg 水平。该研究旨在评估 ALG-020572 在慢性 HBV 感染患者中的安全性和 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: ALG-020572-401 是一项双盲、随机、安慰剂对照试验,由两部分组成。第 1 部分评估了 32 名健康参与者的单剂量,第 2 部分涉及 8 名非肝硬化 HBeAg 阴性、病毒学抑制的慢性 HBV 感染参与者。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究通过单次递增剂量和多次给药对慢性 HBV 感染参与者评估 ALG-020572 的药代动力学、安全性、耐受性和 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 报告的最常见 治疗 相关新发不良事件为注射部位反应。单次剂量的 ALG-020572 在健康受试者中显示出良好的药代动力学和安全性特征。然而,在4名受试者因药物诱导性肝损伤出现显著丙氨酸氨基转移酶升高后,研究被提前终止。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,慢性 HBV 感染参与者对 ALG-020572 的耐受性较差,导致提前终止,并强调开发此类药物需要谨慎。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果提醒人们在开发针对乙型肝炎病毒的反义寡核苷酸时需谨慎,因其存在药物诱导性肝损伤风险,这对未来药物设计和安全性评估具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于安全问题,该研究提前终止,这限制了全面评估长期疗效和安全性的能力。由于样本量有限且提前终止,证据不充分。

title: Next-Generation Sequencing Methods for Sensitive Hepatitis B Viral Genome Analysis: A European Study.
abstract: This multicentre study investigated the utility of next-generation sequencing (NGS) to detect and generate hepatitis B virus (HBV) genomes in samples of low viral load (from 0.2 to 6207 IU/mL). 23 HBV DNA-positive plasma samples of genotypes A-E and one HBV-negative control sample were assayed blindly via 9 established NGS methods from 6 European laboratories. Methods included untargeted metagenomics, pre-enrichment by probe-capture followed by Illumina sequencing, and HBV-specific PCR pre-amplification followed by sequencing with Nanopore or Illumina. Full HBV genomes were obtained only from samples with viral loads > 1000 IU/mL using probe-capture methods, > 200 IU/mL using PCR-Illumina methods, > 10 IU/mL using PCR-Nanopore methods, and in no samples using metagenomic methods. Contamination was observed in the negative control and samples with very low viral loads in PCR-based methods. Probe-capture and metagenomic methods detected additional viruses not routinely screened in blood donations, including polyomaviruses and herpesviruses; positive results were confirmed by PCR. In conclusion, NGS may delineate whole-genome sequences at low viral loads if supported by a PCR pre-amplification step. Probe-capture methods also reliably detect HBV without pre-amplification but show limited genome coverage for samples with low viral loads; they may additionally detect a wide range of blood-borne viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of next-generation sequencing (NGS) in detecting hepatitis B virus (HBV) genomes in samples with low viral loads, addressing the challenge of accurately identifying HBV in clinical settings where viral load is minimal.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicentre study conducted across 6 European laboratories assessed 23 HBV DNA-positive plasma samples of genotypes A-E and one HBV-negative control sample using various NGS methods.
analysis.methods: The study employed untargeted metagenomics, probe-capture followed by Illumina sequencing, and HBV-specific PCR pre-amplification combined with sequencing using either Nanopore or Illumina technologies.
analysis.main_results: Full HBV genomes were successfully obtained from samples with viral loads > 1000 IU/mL using probe-capture methods, > 200 IU/mL using PCR-Illumina methods, and > 10 IU/mL using PCR-Nanopore methods. Metagenomic methods failed to detect HBV in any samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that NGS can effectively generate whole-genome sequences of HBV at low viral loads when supported by a PCR pre-amplification step, highlighting the importance of this approach in improving detection accuracy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings have important implications for enhancing the sensitivity of HBV genome analysis in low viral load scenarios, which can improve diagnostic accuracy and inform better surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are limited by the fact that contamination was observed in negative controls and low viral load samples using PCR-based methods, suggesting potential challenges in interpreting results from such samples.

analysis.summary_en: This European multicentre study evaluated the utility of next-generation sequencing (NGS) in detecting hepatitis B virus (HBV) genomes in samples with low viral loads. The research aimed to address the challenge of accurately identifying HBV in clinical settings where viral load is minimal. Methods included untargeted metagenomics, probe-capture followed by Illumina sequencing, and HBV-specific PCR pre-amplification combined with sequencing using either Nanopore or Illumina technologies. Full HBV genomes were obtained from samples with viral loads > 1000 IU/mL using probe-capture methods, > 200 IU/mL using PCR-Illumina methods, and > 10 IU/mL using PCR-Nanopore methods, while metagenomic methods failed to detect HBV in any samples. The study concluded that NGS can effectively generate whole-genome sequences of HBV at low viral loads when supported by a PCR pre-amplification step, which has important implications for improving diagnostic accuracy and informing better surveillance and treatment strategies. However, the study's results are limited by contamination observed in negative controls and low viral load samples using PCR-based methods, which may affect the reliability of findings in such cases. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the limited sample size and potential for contamination.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估下一代测序 (NGS) 在检测低病毒载量样本中的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 基因组 方面的有效性,解决在病毒载量极低的临床环境中准确识别 HBV 的挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项在 6 个欧洲实验室进行的多中心研究使用各种 NGS 方法评估了 23 份基因型 A-E 的 HBV DNA 阳性血浆样本和一份 HBV 阴性对照样本。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用了非靶向宏基因组学、探针捕获后进行 Illumina 测序,以及 HBV 特异性 PCR 预扩增,并结合使用 Nanopore 或 Illumina 技术进行测序。
elements_zh.main_results: 使用探针捕获方法从病毒载量 > 1000 IU/mL、使用 PCR-Illumina 方法 > 200 IU/mL 和使用 PCR-Nanopore 方法 > 10 IU/mL 的样本中成功获得完整 HBV 基因组。宏基因组方法未能在任何样本中检测到 HBV。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,在 PCR 预扩增步骤的支持下,NGS 可以在低病毒载量下有效生成 HBV 的全 基因组 序列,强调了这种方法在提高检测准确性方面的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对于提高低病毒载量情况下 HBV 基因组 分析的敏感性具有重要意义,这可以提高诊断准确性并为更好的 监测 和 治疗 策略提供信息。

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A multicentre study conducted across 6 European laboratories assessed 23 HBV DNA-positive plasma samples of genotypes A-E and one HBV-negative control sample using various NGS methods.
analysis_en.methods: The study employed untargeted metagenomics, probe-capture followed by Illumina sequencing, and HBV-specific PCR pre-amplification combined with sequencing using either Nanopore or Illumina technologies.
analysis_en.main_results: Full HBV genomes were successfully obtained from samples with viral loads > 1000 IU/mL using probe-capture methods, > 200 IU/mL using PCR-Illumina methods, and > 10 IU/mL using PCR-Nanopore methods. Metagenomic methods failed to detect HBV in any samples.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that NGS can effectively generate whole-genome sequences of HBV at low viral loads when supported by a PCR pre-amplification step, highlighting the importance of this approach in improving detection accuracy.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings have important implications for enhancing the sensitivity of HBV genome analysis in low viral load scenarios, which can improve diagnostic accuracy and inform better surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are limited by the fact that contamination was observed in negative controls and low viral load samples using PCR-based methods, suggesting potential challenges in interpreting results from such samples.

title_zh: 敏感乙型肝炎病毒 基因组 分析的下一代测序方法:一项欧洲研究。
source_body_en: This multicentre study investigated the utility of next-generation sequencing (NGS) to detect and generate hepatitis B virus (HBV) genomes in samples of low viral load (from 0.2 to 6207 IU/mL). 23 HBV DNA-positive plasma samples of genotypes A-E and one HBV-negative control sample were assayed blindly via 9 established NGS methods from 6 European laboratories. Methods included untargeted metagenomics, pre-enrichment by probe-capture followed by Illumina sequencing, and HBV-specific PCR pre-amplification followed by sequencing with Nanopore or Illumina. Full HBV genomes were obtained only from samples with viral loads > 1000 IU/mL using probe-capture methods, > 200 IU/mL using PCR-Illumina methods, > 10 IU/mL using PCR-Nanopore methods, and in no samples using metagenomic methods. Contamination was observed in the negative control and samples with very low viral loads in PCR-based methods. Probe-capture and metagenomic methods detected additional viruses not routinely screened in blood donations, including polyomaviruses and herpesviruses; positive results were confirmed by PCR. In conclusion, NGS may delineate whole-genome sequences at low viral loads if supported by a PCR pre-amplification step. Probe-capture methods also reliably detect HBV without pre-amplification but show limited genome coverage for samples with low viral loads; they may additionally detect a wide range of blood-borne viruses.

title: Barriers to Hepatitis B Treatment: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Registry and Survey Study by the Canadian Hepatitis B Network.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide, yet treatment uptake is suboptimal even in high-resource settings. This pan-Canadian study aimed to quantify treatment gaps within the Canadian Hepatitis B Network (CanHepB) Registry, compare characteristics of treatment-eligible but untreated patients to those receiving therapy, and assess patient and specialist perspectives on barriers to treatment. METHODS: A cross-sectional, retrospective analysis of 1983 adults with CHB followed in 18 Canadian hepatitis B specialty clinics between January 2018 and November 2024. Treatment eligibility was determined using the 2018 Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver guidelines. An anonymous survey captured patient-reported barriers and perspectives (n = 191), while a separate survey evaluated specialist perceptions (n = 54). RESULTS: Among 881 untreated patients, 46.4% (n = 409) were treatment eligible. Compared with the treatment group (n = 1087), the treatment-eligible but untreated patients were younger (median 47.3 vs. 54.5 years), more frequently female (54.2% vs. 39.7%), and more likely to be of Black/African/Caribbean origin (18.2% vs. They had a lower prevalence of cirrhosis (2.4% vs. 20.3%), HCC (0.7% vs. 9.3%), and hypertension (17.1% vs. 22.9%), but a higher prevalence of steatotic liver disease (36.4% vs. 24.6%) and dyslipidemia (14.7% vs. Among untreated respondents, concerns included side effects, the need for long-term therapy, and lack of curative options. Conversely, specialists identified cost as the primary barrier and side effects as the least concerning. CONCLUSION: This nationwide study reveals a significant treatment gap in CHB care, driven by demographic disparities and a mismatch between patient concerns and clinician perceptions.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adults within a high-resource setting, focusing on treatment eligibility, demographic disparities among untreated patients, and the mismatch between patient-reported barriers and specialist perceptions regarding HBV therapy.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a cross-sectional, retrospective analysis of 1983 adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) enrolled in 18 Canadian specialty clinics from January 2018 to November 2024, using the 2018 Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver guidelines to determine treatment eligibility.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 881 untreated patients, 46.4% (n=409) were treatment eligible, with untreated treatment-eligible patients being younger, more frequently female, and more likely to be of Black/African/Caribbean origin compared to treated patients. Untreated patients had lower prevalence of cirrhosis, HCC, and hypertension but higher prevalence of steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Patient concerns about side effects, long-term therapy, and lack of curative options contrasted with specialists' identification of cost as the primary barrier and side effects as the least concerning, highlighting a mismatch in perceived barriers to HBV treatment.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study underscores the need for targeted interventions to address demographic disparities in HBV treatment uptake and to align patient and specialist perspectives on barriers to improve CHB care in high-resource settings.

analysis.summary_en: This pan-Canadian cross-sectional study of 1983 adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in 18 specialty clinics from 2018 to 2024 quantified a significant treatment gap, with 46.4% of untreated patients (n=409) meeting eligibility criteria. Treatment-eligible but untreated patients were younger, more often female, and more likely to be of Black/African/Caribbean origin than treated patients, while having lower rates of cirrhosis, HCC, and hypertension but higher rates of steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia. Patient-reported barriers included concerns about side effects, long-term therapy, and lack of curative options, whereas specialists identified cost as the primary barrier and side effects as least concerning. These findings reveal demographic disparities and a mismatch between patient and clinician perspectives that impede optimal CHB management.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在 881 名未经治疗的患者中,46.4% (n=409) 符合 治疗 条件,与接受治疗的患者相比,未经治疗的 治疗 患者更年轻,女性居多,而且更有可能是黑人/非洲/加勒比裔。未经治疗的患者肝硬化、肝癌和高血压的 患病率 较低,但脂肪肝疾病和血脂异常的 患病率 较高。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines human chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in adults within a high-resource setting, focusing on treatment eligibility, demographic disparities among untreated patients, and the mismatch between patient-reported barriers and specialist perceptions regarding HBV therapy.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a cross-sectional, retrospective analysis of 1983 adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) enrolled in 18 Canadian specialty clinics from January 2018 to November 2024, using the 2018 Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver guidelines to determine treatment eligibility.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 881 untreated patients, 46.4% (n=409) were treatment eligible, with untreated treatment-eligible patients being younger, more frequently female, and more likely to be of Black/African/Caribbean origin compared to treated patients. Untreated patients had lower prevalence of cirrhosis, HCC, and hypertension but higher prevalence of steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Patient concerns about side effects, long-term therapy, and lack of curative options contrasted with specialists' identification of cost as the primary barrier and side effects as the least concerning, highlighting a mismatch in perceived barriers to HBV treatment.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The study underscores the need for targeted interventions to address demographic disparities in HBV treatment uptake and to align patient and specialist perspectives on barriers to improve CHB care in high-resource settings.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎的障碍 治疗:加拿大乙型肝炎网络进行的多中心横断面登记和调查研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide, yet treatment uptake is suboptimal even in high-resource settings. This pan-Canadian study aimed to quantify treatment gaps within the Canadian Hepatitis B Network (CanHepB) Registry, compare characteristics of treatment-eligible but untreated patients to those receiving therapy, and assess patient and specialist perspectives on barriers to treatment. METHODS: A cross-sectional, retrospective analysis of 1983 adults with CHB followed in 18 Canadian hepatitis B specialty clinics between January 2018 and November 2024. Treatment eligibility was determined using the 2018 Canadian Association for the Study of the Liver guidelines. An anonymous survey captured patient-reported barriers and perspectives (n = 191), while a separate survey evaluated specialist perceptions (n = 54). RESULTS: Among 881 untreated patients, 46.4% (n = 409) were treatment eligible. Compared with the treatment group (n = 1087), the treatment-eligible but untreated patients were younger (median 47.3 vs. 54.5 years), more frequently female (54.2% vs. 39.7%), and more likely to be of Black/African/Caribbean origin (18.2% vs. They had a lower prevalence of cirrhosis (2.4% vs. 20.3%), HCC (0.7% vs. 9.3%), and hypertension (17.1% vs. 22.9%), but a higher prevalence of steatotic liver disease (36.4% vs. 24.6%) and dyslipidemia (14.7% vs. Among untreated respondents, concerns included side effects, the need for long-term therapy, and lack of curative options. Conversely, specialists identified cost as the primary barrier and side effects as the least concerning. CONCLUSION: This nationwide study reveals a significant treatment gap in CHB care, driven by demographic disparities and a mismatch between patient concerns and clinician perceptions.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的:慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 仍然是全世界肝硬化和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 的主要原因,但即使在资源丰富的环境中,治疗 的摄取也不是最佳的。这项泛加拿大研究旨在量化加拿大乙型肝炎网络 (CanHepB) 注册中心内的 治疗 差距,比较符合 治疗 资格但未经治疗的患者与正在接受治疗的患者的特征,并评估患者和专家对 治疗 障碍的看法。方法:对 2018 年 1 月至 2024 年 11 月期间加拿大 18 个乙型肝炎专科诊所的 1983 名成人慢性乙型肝炎患者进行横断面回顾性分析。治疗 资格是根据 2018 年加拿大肝脏研究协会指南确定的。一项匿名调查记录了患者报告的障碍和观点 (n = 191),而另一项调查评估了专家的看法 (n = 54)。结果:在 881 名未经治疗的患者中,46.4% (n = 409) 符合 治疗 资格。与 治疗 组 (n = 1087) 相比,符合 治疗 条件但未接受治疗的患者更年轻(中位年龄 47.3 岁 vs. 54.5 岁),女性更常见(54.2% vs. 39.7%),并且更有可能是黑人/非洲/加勒比裔(18.2% vs. 他们的 患病率 较低)肝硬化(2.4% vs. 20.3%)、肝癌(0.7% vs. 9.3%)和高血压(17.1% vs. 22.9%),但脂肪变性肝病(36.4% vs. 24.6%)和血脂异常(14.7% vs. 未治疗的受访者)的 患病率 较高。在未治疗的受访者中,担忧包括副作用、需要长期治疗以及缺乏治疗。相反,专家认为成本是主要障碍,而副作用是最不令人担忧的。这项全国性研究揭示了慢性乙型肝炎护理中存在显着的 治疗 差距,这是由人口差异以及患者关注点和临床医生认知之间的不匹配造成的。

title: Evaluation of the Virucidal Activity of Chlorine Dioxide against Hepatitis B Virus
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global public health concern, with numerous nosocomial and occupational outbreaks reported. Preventing indirect HBV transmission through effective disinfection is crucial. This study evaluated the virucidal activity of chlorine dioxide (ClO2) against HBV and compared it with sodium hypochlorite (NaClO). Pretreatment of HBV with ClO2 at 10, 100, and 250 ppm (mg/L) for 1 min reduced hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) release to 65.5%, 21.9%, and 7.0%; hepatitis B core (HBc)-positive cells to 59.1%, 27.0%, and 6.6%; intracellular HBV RNA to 71.5%, 31.6%, and 3.0%; and extracellular HBV DNA to 82.2%, 42.6%, and 14.1%, respectively. At identical concentrations, NaClO produced smaller reductions. In the presence of organic matter, no significant reduction in ClO2 activity against HBV was observed. ClO2 demonstrated approximately 2.2-fold greater anti-HBV potency than NaClO with and without bovine serum albumin and sheep erythrocytes. Neutralizer, cell-permissiveness, and ultrafiltration controls supported direct viral inactivation. These findings indicate that ClO2 showed stronger in vitro anti-HBV activity than NaClO within the tested concentration range and conditions.

title: Attendance Among People With Hepatitis B in UK Secondary Care: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Chronic Hepatitis B disease requires lifelong monitoring to prevent complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite structured care pathways, non-attendance within UK secondary care remains challenging. This scoping review aimed to synthesise existing evidence on factors influencing non-attendance at secondary care appointments and strategies to improve appointment adherence among people living with Chronic Hepatitis B. Eligibility Criteria: Peer-reviewed sources examining adults with Hepatitis B attendance at UK secondary care services. Grey literature was excluded. Sources of Evidence: Searches were performed in CINAHL Ultimate, Medline, Embase, Scopus and APA PsycINFO. Data were charted using a structured data extraction form and synthesised narratively. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria. Identified barriers included patient-related factors (e.g., limited health literacy, stigmatisation, competing priorities), system-level challenges (e.g., appointment scheduling and accessibility) and cultural or language barriers. Psychological factors, including fear of diagnosis and treatment side effects, were also reported. Reported strategies included patient education, culturally tailored interventions, reminder systems (e.g., SMS and telephone calls) and integrated care models involving community outreach. Non-attendance among people with chronic Hepatitis B in secondary care is influenced by a complex interplay of personal, social and systemic factors. Interventions that address multiple barriers, particularly those that incorporate culturally sensitive approaches and reminder systems, may improve engagement. Further research is needed to co-design and evaluate interventions with affected communities.

title: Hepatitis B and C Prevention, Screening, and Diagnostic Services at HIV Treatment Sites: International Epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prevention, screening, and diagnostic services for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) can prevent morbidity and mortality in people receiving HIV care. However, there is limited information about the availability of HBV and HCV services at HIV clinics globally. METHODS: The International epidemiology Databases to Evaluate AIDS (IeDEA) conducted surveys of service delivery and practices at participating HIV treatment centers from 7 regions. We used 2023 survey data to measure availability of HBV vaccination, HBV and HCV screening, HBV surface antigen (HBsAg), HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to test associations of site characteristics with HBV and HCV services. RESULTS: HBV vaccination was available on-site at 67.7% of 204 HIV treatment sites. Screening for HBV and HCV at HIV care enrollment was reported by 72.1% and 50% of sites, respectively. HBsAg, HBV DNA, HCV antibody, and HCV RNA testing were available on-site at 77%, 47.6%, 61.8%, and 44.6% of sites, respectively. Sites serving predominately rural (vs. urban) populations were less likely to report on-site availability of HBV DNA [odds ratio (OR):0.07; 95% confidence interval: 0.01 to 0.68; P = 0.02], HCV antibody (OR = 0.18; 95% CI: 0.04 to 0.92; P = 0.04), and HCV RNA (OR = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.90; P = 0.04) testing. CONCLUSION: Life-saving services such as HBV vaccination, HBsAg, and HCV antibody testing were available on-site at most HIV treatment sites participating in the IeDEA network. Lower availability at rural sites suggests that expansion of services is important to eliminate HBV and HCV as public health problems in people receiving HIV care.

title: Metabolic Risk Factors of Developing Liver Steatosis among Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B: A National Cohort from Romania
abstract: Background and Aims: The coexistence of liver steatosis in patients with chronic viral hepatitis B (CHB) is growing relevant as the global epidemic of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The aim of this study was to identify the metabolic risk factors linked to steatotic liver disease (SLD) in Romanian patients with CHB. Methods: In this prospective study, we evaluated 320,000 individuals in the LIVE(RO)2 nationwide screening program in Romania from 2021 to 2023. The majority of the patients had undergone transient elastography using controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) to diagnose liver steatosis, and they belonged to vulnerable categories. Exclusion criteria included heavy alcohol consumption, any other liver disease unrelated to CHB, and the lack of CAP evaluation. Results: 5,321 individuals (1.67%) were found with CHB in the screening program. In the final analysis we included 1,970 patients, with a mean age of 55.87±13.84 years; 57.9% of them were males, with a mean body mass index (BMI) level of 27.26 kg/m2, and 61.9% of the patients were vulnerable. The prevalence of SLD was 42.2% in the group of vulnerable individuals, compared with non-vulnerable participants, who had a prevalence of SLD of 26.4%. Moreover, patients with vulnerable conditions have a higher prevalence of T2DM (11.5%), hypertension (41.3%), and raised BMI levels ≥25 kg/m2 (71.3%). In our study, vulnerable subjects had a higher prevalence of hepatitis B virus e antigen (HBeAg) positivity of 3%, and it was found to be a protective risk factor for hepatic steatosis development (aOR=0.397). Also, these patients had a higher prevalence of severe liver fibrosis (≥ F3) of 17.1%, compared with those non-vulnerable, with a prevalence of 9.7% of severe liver fibrosis. More than that, we find that the presence of HBeAg-positive increases the risk of severe liver fibrosis progression 6 times higher. Conclusions: In our study we found a prevalence of hepatic steatosis of 42.2% in the cohort of vulnerable untreated patients with CHB, and the prevalence of severe fibrosis was 17.1%. Presence of HBeAg-positive was found to be a protective risk factor for hepatic steatosis but accelerates the development of severe fibrosis along with T2DM, which is more common in the vulnerable CHB cohort.

The aim of this study was to identify the metabolic risk factors linked to steatotic liver disease (SLD) in Romanian patients with CHB. Methods: In this prospective study, we evaluated 320,000 individuals in the LIVE(RO)2 nationwide screening program in Romania from 2021 to 2023. The majority of the patients had undergone transient elastography using controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) to diagnose liver steatosis, and they belonged to vulnerable categories. Exclusion criteria included heavy alcohol consumption, any other liver disease unrelated to CHB, and the lack of CAP evaluation. Results: 5,321 individuals (1.67%) were found with CHB in the screening program. In the final analysis we included 1,970 patients, with a mean age of 55.87±13.84 years; 57.9% of them were males, with a mean body mass index (BMI) level of 27.26 kg/m2, and 61.9% of the patients were vulnerable. The prevalence of SLD was 42.2% in the group of vulnerable individuals, compared with non-vulnerable participants, who had a prevalence of SLD of 26.4%. Moreover, patients with vulnerable conditions have a higher prevalence of T2DM (11.5%), hypertension (41.3%), and raised BMI levels ≥25 kg/m2 (71.3%). In our study, vulnerable subjects had a higher prevalence of hepatitis B virus e antigen (HBeAg) positivity of 3%, and it was found to be a protective risk factor for hepatic steatosis development (aOR=0.397). Also, these patients had a higher prevalence of severe liver fibrosis (≥ F3) of 17.1%, compared with those non-vulnerable, with a prevalence of 9.7% of severe liver fibrosis. More than that, we find that the presence of HBeAg-positive increases the risk of severe liver fibrosis progression 6 times higher. Conclusions: In our study we found a prevalence of hepatic steatosis of 42.2% in the cohort of vulnerable untreated patients with CHB, and the prevalence of severe fibrosis was 17.1%. Presence of HBeAg-positive was found to be a protective risk factor for hepatic steatosis but accelerates the development of severe fibrosis along with T2DM, which is more common in the vulnerable CHB cohort.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the metabolic risk factors associated with liver steatosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in Romania. It highlights that vulnerable individuals with CHB have a significantly higher prevalence of steatosis (42.2%) and severe fibrosis (17.1%) compared to non-vulnerable participants (26.4% and 9.7%, respectively). However, the study's observational design and potential confounding factors limit the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

abstract_zh: 背景与目的:随着全球肥胖和2型糖尿病(T2DM)流行病的发展,慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者中肝脂肪变性的共存现象日益受到关注。本研究旨在识别罗马尼亚CHB患者中脂肪性肝病(SLD)相关的代谢风险因素。方法:本项前瞻性研究纳入罗马尼亚LIVE(RO)2全国筛查项目(2021-2023年)的320,000名受试者。大多数患者接受了控制性衰减参数(CAP)瞬时弹性成像检查以诊断肝脂肪变性,且属于脆弱人群。排除标准包括重度饮酒、任何与CHB无关的其他肝病以及缺乏CAP评估。结果:筛查项目中发现5,321名个体(1.67%)患有CHB。最终分析纳入1,970名患者,平均年龄为55.87±13.84岁;其中57.9%为男性,平均体质指数(BMI)水平为27.26 kg/m2,61.9%的患者属于脆弱人群。SLD的患病率在脆弱个体中为42.2%,而在非脆弱参与者中为26.4%。此外,脆弱条件患者的T2DM(11.5%)、高血压(41.3%)和BMI≥25 kg/m2(71.3%)患病率更高。本研究中,脆弱受试者HBeAg阳性率为3%,并被发现是肝脂肪变性发展的保护性风险因素(校正优势比[aOR]=0.397)。这些患者重度肝纤维化(≥F3)的患病率也更高,为17.1%,而非脆弱者为9.7%。此外,HBeAg阳性的存在可使重度肝纤维化进展风险提高6倍。结论:本研究发现,在未经治疗的CHB脆弱患者中,肝脂肪变性的患病率为42.2%,重度纤维化的患病率为17.1%。HBeAg阳性被发现是肝脂肪变性的保护性风险因素,但会加速重度纤维化的发展,且T2DM在CHB脆弱人群中更为常见。

title: Risk-based hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance thresholds using a prediction score in Asian patients with chronic hepatitis B: a nationwide cohort study
abstract: BACKGROUNDS/AIMS: This study aimed to quantify hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence according to a validated prediction score and to define score-based cut-offs corresponding to surveillance-relevant incidence thresholds in Asian patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) receiving antiviral therapy. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Adults with CHB initiating nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy between 2012 and 2023 were included, hose with viral coinfections, prior malignancy, or decompensated cirrhosis were excluded. HCC risk was stratified using the HCC-RESCUE score. Incident HCC was the primary outcome. Annual HCC incidence rates and adjusted hazard ratios were estimated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Among 199,143 treated patients (median follow-up, 7.3 years), 15,233 developed HCC. Adjusted annual HCC incidence increased progressively across risk strata: 0.31% (95% CI 0.24-0.40) in the low-risk group, 1.09% (0.84-1.41) in the intermediate-risk group, and 1.85% (1.44-2.40) in the high-risk group. abstract_zh: 背景/目的:本研究旨在根据经过验证的预测评分量化肝细胞癌 (HCC) 发病率,并定义接受 抗病毒药物 治疗的亚洲 监测 (CHB) 患者中与 监测 相关 发病率 阈值相对应的基于评分的截止值。方法:我们利用韩国国民健康保险服务数据库进行了一项全国范围内的 队列研究 研究。纳入 2012 年至 2023 年间开始核苷(酸)类似物治疗的 CHB 成人,排除病毒合并感染、既往恶性肿瘤或失代偿性肝硬化。使用 HCC-RESCUE 评分对 HCC 风险进行分层。HCC 事件是主要结局。使用多变量 Cox 比例风险模型估算年度 HCC 发病率 率和调整后的风险比。结果:在 199,143 名接受治疗的患者中(中位随访时间为 7.3 年),15,233 名患者发展为 HCC。调整后的年度 HCC 发病率 在不同风险层中逐渐增加:低风险组为 0.31% (95% CI 0.24-0.40),中风险组为 1.09% (0.84-1.41),高风险组为 1.85% (1.44-2.40)。与低风险组相比,中风险组和高风险组的 HCC 调整后风险比分别为 3.48 (95% CI 3.35-3.61) 和 5.90 (5.62-6.19)(均 p<0.001)。对应于年度 HCC 发病率 阈值 0.2%、1.5% 和 3.0% 的 HCC-RESCUE 评分分别为 47、66 和 90。结论:在大量接受 发病率 治疗的亚洲 CHB 人群中,基于预测评分的分层揭示了残余 HCC 风险的分级谱,并确定了与监测。这些发现支持 HCC 监测 策略的 发病率 知情细化,补充了 抗病毒药物 治疗 时代传统的基于肝硬化的标准。

title: Natural immune escape mutations in the envelope proteins of hepatitis B virus (HBV) regulate the assembly and infectivity of human hepatitis delta virus (HDV)
abstract: ABSTRACT The study examined how 35 natural immune escape mutations (IEMs) of hepatitis B virus (HBV) located in the major antigenic loop (MAL) of the envelope proteins regulate the assembly and infectivity of the natural sub-viral agent of HBV, hepatitis delta virus (HDV). All IEMs were permissive for the assembly and secretion of HDV virions. Only seven IEMs resulted in considerably decreased levels of secreted HDV virions in the context of one to three tested HBV genotypes, B, C, or D. The effects of IEMs on HDV infectivity were much more pronounced than on the assembly. Thirteen IEMs considerably inhibited the infectivity of HDV virions. All of them greatly reduced both the levels of HDV RNA genomes accumulated in the infected cells and the percentage of HDV-infected cells. Only one mutant R(169)P generated completely non-infectious HDV virions. Our analysis of the IEMs-mediated effects on the HDV life cycle therefore identified a number of critically important amino acid residues in the MAL, and aided the mechanistic understanding of the MAL functioning during the processes of HDV assembly and infectivity. The inhibition of either HDV assembly and/or infectivity is expected to suppress the viral spread and super-infection in vivo , and therefore to reduce the HDV reservoir in infected livers. Overall, the generated data showed that the anti-HBV immune response is capable of considerable down-regulation of the concomitant HDV infection by facilitating the selection for IEMs in the MAL. The study further advanced our understanding of the mechanisms of the complex HBV-HDV and HDV-host interactions. IMPORTANCE The study demonstrated that anti-hepatitis B virus (HBV) immune response via selection for the immune escape mutations (IEMs) in HBV envelope proteins (surface antigen, HBsAg) can considerably reduce the assembly and/or infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) virions coated with HBsAg. The IEMs could down-regulate concomitant HDV infection mostly via affecting HDV infectivity, which was considerably inhibited by 13 out of 35 IEMs. The HDV spread/super-infection, which are expected to be suppressed by inhibited via HBV-specific IEMs the assembly and/or infectivity of HDV virions, should result in a reduced HDV reservoir in infected livers. The examination of the inhibition of HDV infectivity by IEMs apparently indicated that the major antigenic loop (MAL) of HBsAg could contain the residues primarily involved in viral attachment/entry and also the residues mostly regulating intracellular post-entry trafficking of HDV virions. The data advance our understanding of the MAL functioning during infection and of the indirect regulation of the HDV life cycle through the anti-HBV immune response.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how natural immune escape mutations (IEMs) in the envelope proteins of hepatitis B virus (HBV) affect the assembly and infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV). The background highlights the importance of understanding these interactions to better comprehend the mechanisms of immune evasion and their impact on HDV.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 35 natural immune escape mutations (IEMs) of HBV located in the major antigenic loop (MAL) of the envelope proteins. These mutations were tested in the context of one to three HBV genotypes, B, C, or D, to assess their effects on HDV assembly and infectivity.
analysis.methods: The researchers examined the effects of IEMs on HDV virion assembly and infectivity by assessing secreted HDV virion levels and HDV RNA genome accumulation in infected cells. They also evaluated the percentage of HDV-infected cells and the infectivity of HDV virions in the presence of these mutations.
analysis.main_results: Only seven IEMs resulted in considerably decreased levels of secreted HDV virions. Thirteen IEMs considerably inhibited HDV infectivity, greatly reducing both HDV RNA genomes accumulated in infected cells and the percentage of HDV-infected cells. One mutant, R(169)P, generated completely non-infectious HDV virions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that IEMs in HBV can significantly down-regulate HDV infectivity, which is more pronounced than their effect on HDV assembly. This provides novel insights into the role of the MAL in HDV life cycle regulation and the potential of anti-HBV immune responses to influence HDV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results contribute to the mechanistic understanding of HBV-HDV interactions and may inform strategies for targeting HDV through HBV-specific immune responses, potentially aiding in the development of therapies or vaccines that reduce HDV reservoirs in infected livers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on in vitro analysis of HBV genotypes and their effects on HDV, which may limit generalizability to in vivo conditions. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of direct clinical or epidemiological data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how natural immune escape mutations (IEMs) in the envelope proteins of hepatitis B virus (HBV) influence the assembly and infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV). It identifies that while all IEMs are permissive for HDV virion assembly, only seven significantly reduce secreted HDV levels. Thirteen IEMs inhibit HDV infectivity, with one mutant, R(169)P, generating completely non-infectious virions. The findings suggest that IEMs primarily affect HDV infectivity, which is more pronounced than their impact on assembly. This provides insights into the role of the major antigenic loop (MAL) in HDV life cycle regulation and highlights the potential of anti-HBV immune responses to suppress HDV infection. The study's results are of moderate strength due to their in vitro nature and limited in vivo data.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 包膜蛋白中的自然免疫逃逸 突变 调节人丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 的组装和感染性
source_body_en: ABSTRACT The study examined how 35 natural immune escape mutations (IEMs) of hepatitis B virus (HBV) located in the major antigenic loop (MAL) of the envelope proteins regulate the assembly and infectivity of the natural sub-viral agent of HBV, hepatitis delta virus (HDV). All IEMs were permissive for the assembly and secretion of HDV virions. Only seven IEMs resulted in considerably decreased levels of secreted HDV virions in the context of one to three tested HBV genotypes, B, C, or D. The effects of IEMs on HDV infectivity were much more pronounced than on the assembly. Thirteen IEMs considerably inhibited the infectivity of HDV virions. All of them greatly reduced both the levels of HDV RNA genomes accumulated in the infected cells and the percentage of HDV-infected cells. Only one mutant R(169)P generated completely non-infectious HDV virions. Our analysis of the IEMs-mediated effects on the HDV life cycle therefore identified a number of critically important amino acid residues in the MAL, and aided the mechanistic understanding of the MAL functioning during the processes of HDV assembly and infectivity. The inhibition of either HDV assembly and/or infectivity is expected to suppress the viral spread and super-infection in vivo , and therefore to reduce the HDV reservoir in infected livers. Overall, the generated data showed that the anti-HBV immune response is capable of considerable down-regulation of the concomitant HDV infection by facilitating the selection for IEMs in the MAL. The study further advanced our understanding of the mechanisms of the complex HBV-HDV and HDV-host interactions. IMPORTANCE The study demonstrated that anti-hepatitis B virus (HBV) immune response via selection for the immune escape mutations (IEMs) in HBV envelope proteins (surface antigen, HBsAg) can considerably reduce the assembly and/or infectivity of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) virions coated with HBsAg. The IEMs could down-regulate concomitant HDV infection mostly via affecting HDV infectivity, which was considerably inhibited by 13 out of 35 IEMs. The HDV spread/super-infection, which are expected to be suppressed by inhibited via HBV-specific IEMs the assembly and/or infectivity of HDV virions, should result in a reduced HDV reservoir in infected livers. The examination of the inhibition of HDV infectivity by IEMs apparently indicated that the major antigenic loop (MAL) of HBsAg could contain the residues primarily involved in viral attachment/entry and also the residues mostly regulating intracellular post-entry trafficking of HDV virions. The data advance our understanding of the MAL functioning during infection and of the indirect regulation of the HDV life cycle through the anti-HBV immune response.
abstract_zh: 摘要:该研究探讨了位于包膜蛋白主要抗原环(MAL)中的 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)的 35 个自然免疫逃逸 突变(IEM)如何调节 HBV 天然亚病毒因子——丁型肝炎病毒(HDV)的组装和感染性。所有 IEM 都允许 HDV 病毒颗粒的组装和分泌。在一到三种测试的 HBV 基因型(B、C 或 D)的背景下,只有 7 个 IEM 导致分泌的 HDV 病毒体水平显着降低。IEM 对 HDV 感染性的影响比对装配的影响要显着得多。13 个 IEM 显着抑制了 HDV 病毒粒子的感染性。它们都大大降低了感染细胞中积累的 HDV RNA 基因组 水平和 HDV 感染细胞的百分比。只有一种突变体 R(169)P 产生完全非传染性的 HDV 病毒体。因此,我们对 IEM 介导的 HDV 生命周期影响的分析确定了 MAL 中的许多至关重要的氨基酸残基,并有助于理解 HDV 组装和感染过程中 MAL 功能的机制。HDV组装和/或感染性的抑制有望抑制体内病毒传播和重复感染,从而减少受感染肝脏中的HDV 储存宿主。总体而言,生成的数据表明,抗 HBV 免疫应答 能够通过促进 MAL 中 IEM 的选择,从而显着下调伴随的 HDV 感染。该研究进一步加深了我们对 HBV-HDV 和 HDV-宿主 复杂相互作用机制的理解。重要性 该研究表明,通过选择 HBV 包膜蛋白(表面抗原,HBsAg)中的免疫逃逸 免疫应答 (IEM),抗 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 免疫应答 可以显着减少 HBsAg 包被的丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 病毒体的组装和/或感染性。IEM 可以主要通过影响 HDV 感染性来下调伴随的 HDV 感染,35 个 IEM 中有 13 个显着抑制了 HDV 感染性。HDV 传播/重复感染预计可通过 HBV 特异性 IEM 抑制 HDV 病毒粒子的组装和/或感染性来抑制,从而导致受感染肝脏中 HDV 储存宿主 减少。IEM 对 HDV 感染性抑制的检查显然表明 HBsAg 的主要抗原环 (MAL) 可能含有主要参与病毒附着/进入的残基,以及主要调节 HDV 病毒粒子进入细胞内后运输的残基。这些数据加深了我们对感染期间 MAL 功能以及通过抗 HBV 免疫应答 间接调节 HDV 生命周期的理解。

title: Immunization and the hepatitis B virus: A view from the ESPGHAN Hepatology Committee
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a global health challenge, with more than 250 million people chronically infected worldwide and >2000 daily deaths from HBV‐related disease. Early‐life acquisition is the primary driver of chronic infection; up to 90% of infants infected perinatally progress to chronic HBV infection compared with markedly lower rates in older children and adults. Universal infant immunization, including the birth‐dose, has been central to global elimination, resulting in a substantial reduction in chronic HBV infection, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Recent statements from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention question the evidence‐base for early‐life vaccination and recommend deferring HBV immunization until later in childhood. These claims reflect misconceptions about HBV epidemiology and reference a perceived association between infant vaccination and autism. This communication summarizes evidence demonstrating the risks of early‐life HBV transmission leading to chronic infection. We argue that delaying or foregoing immunization would leave infants at unnecessary risk. We reference two decades of research in which large‐scale studies have not identified an association between vaccination, including HBV vaccination, and autism.
journal: Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition

title: Peripheral Biomarkers in Chronic Hepatitis D Infection: A Review.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis D represents the most severe form of viral hepatitis and is associated with higher rates of advanced fibrosis, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma than hepatitis B monoinfection. It is caused by the hepatitis D virus (HDV), a defective RNA virus that requires co-infection with hepatitis B (HBV) for hepatocyte entry and propagation. Accurate prediction of liver disease sequelae and treatment response using currently available serological biomarkers remains challenging. This article reviews peripheral biomarkers in HDV, including novel biomarkers of HBV activity, exploring their potential clinical utility and areas for future development. Peripheral biomarkers capable of risk stratifying patients with HDV, monitoring or predicting treatment response and elucidating the natural history of infection (including the complex relationship with HBV), would enable individualised care and early identification of those at greater risk of developing advanced liver disease. Establishing the role of these biomarkers in larger, ethnically diverse populations both on existing treatments and in the context of emerging antiviral therapies will be imperative going forward.

title: The Evolving Burden of Hepatitis B and C: Past Trends and Future Projections from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B and C continue to pose significant challenges to global public health, and this study is aimed at evaluating their burden. METHODS: Leveraging data from the Global Burden of Disease 2021, we analyzed age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) and age-standardized disability-adjusted life year rates (ASDRs) for hepatitis B and C from 1990 to 2021 using Joinpoint regression, age-period-cohort models, and decomposition analysis. Bayesian age-period-cohort models were applied to project future trends up to 2036. Additionally, we assessed the burden attributable to modifiable risk factors and its association with socioeconomic indicators. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2021, the global ASMR for hepatitis B declined from 12.19 to 7.57 per 100,000, and the ASMR for hepatitis C decreased from 8.18 to 6.10 per 100,000. Despite these decreases, the absolute numbers of deaths and DALYs continued to increase, mainly driven by population growth and aging. In 2021, males carried a disproportionately higher burden of hepatitis B and C compared to females. Moreover, countries with low socioeconomic development faced a greater burden. Notably, high alcohol consumption accounted for 16.20% of hepatitis B DALYs, while drug use was responsible for 49.49% of hepatitis C DALYs. By 2036, ASMRs are projected to decline further to 5.90 per 100,000 for hepatitis B and 5.23 per 100,000 for hepatitis C. CONCLUSIONS: Although ASMRs and ASDRs have declined, the global burden of hepatitis B and C remains considerable. Continued efforts in vaccination, antiviral treatment, and control of key risk factors are crucial, especially in populations with a high burden.

abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎继续对全球公共卫生构成重大挑战,本研究旨在评估其负担。方法:利用 2021 年全球疾病负担的数据,我们使用 Joinpoint 回归、年龄周期 队列研究 模型和分解分析,分析了 1990 年至 2021 年乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎的年龄标准化 死亡率 率 (ASMR) 和年龄标准化伤残调整生命年率 (ASDR)。应用贝叶斯年龄周期 队列研究 模型来预测截至 2036 年的未来趋势。此外,我们评估了可改变的风险因素造成的负担及其与社会经济指标的关联。结果:从1990年到2021年,全球乙型肝炎ASMR从每10万人12.19下降到7.57,丙型肝炎ASMR从每10万人8.18下降到6.10。尽管出现这些下降,但死亡人数和伤残调整生命年的绝对人数继续增加,这主要是由人口增长和老龄化推动的。2021 年,与女性相比,男性的乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎负担要高得多。此外,社会经济发展水平较低的国家面临着更大的负担。值得注意的是,大量饮酒占乙型肝炎 DALY 的 16.20%,而吸毒则占丙型肝炎 DALY 的 49.49%。到 2036 年,乙型肝炎 ASMR 预计将进一步下降至每 100,000 人 5.90,丙型肝炎则进一步下降至每 100,000 人 5.23。结论:尽管 ASMR 和 ASDR 有所下降,但乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎的全球负担仍然相当大。继续努力疫苗接种、抗病毒药物、治疗以及控制关键风险因素至关重要,特别是在高负担人群中。

title: Trends in Comorbidities and Fatalities Among First-Time Hepatitis B Hospitalizations in Poland (2012-2023).
abstract: BACKGROUND The clinical profile of patients hospitalized with hepatitis B virus (HBV) is increasingly influenced by coexisting conditions and death patterns. This study aimed to assess comorbidities and fatality rates among patients hospitalized for the first time with HBV between 2012 and 2023. MATERIAL AND METHODS A 12-year retrospective nationwide analysis of first-time HBV hospitalizations in Poland was conducted using data from the Nationwide General Hospital Morbidity Study. RESULTS Digestive diseases (15.6%), cardiovascular diseases (10.5%), and endocrine and metabolic disorders (9.6%) were the most prevalent comorbidities. Between 2012 and 2023, marked increases were observed in digestive (12.3%-27.4%) and metabolic (8.5%-18.5%) disorders, while circulatory diseases rose from 7.4% to 18.6% with post-2019 stabilization. Immune-related and genitourinary disorders demonstrated sustained post-2019 growth, whereas several categories, including neoplasms and respiratory diseases, showed growth-decline patterns. Hypertension and liver fibrosis were the most frequent individual diagnoses, with sustained or stepwise increases over time. Age-stratified analyses revealed a shift from infection-related conditions in younger patients toward cardiometabolic and advanced hepatic diseases in older groups. Fatality rates increased from 6.8-15.9 per 1000 hospitalizations (2012-2019) to 23.1-30.7 per 1000 (2020-2023), peaking during 2020-2021, with higher mortality in men. CONCLUSIONS First-time HBV hospitalizations are increasingly characterized by multimorbidity and rising fatality rates, particularly in older patients. These findings highlight a growing clinical and public health burden, underscoring the need for integrated, age-tailored management and improved surveillance to reduce mortality and optimize HBV care.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估 2012 年至 2023 年间首次因 HBV 住院的患者的合并症和死亡率。乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 住院患者的临床特征越来越受到共存疾病和死亡模式的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 利用全国综合医院发病率研究的数据,对波兰首次 HBV 住院患者进行了 12 年全国回顾性分析。该研究纳入了 2012 年至 2023 年间首次因 HBV 住院的患者。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用全国综合医院发病率研究的数据来分析首次乙肝住院患者的合并症和死亡率。进行年龄分层分析以确定不同条件下 患病率 的趋势。
elements_zh.main_results: 消化系统疾病(15.6%)、心血管疾病(10.5%)以及内分泌和代谢紊乱(9.6%)是最常见的合并症。免疫相关疾病和泌尿生殖系统疾病在 2019 年后呈现持续增长,而包括肿瘤和呼吸系统疾病在内的几个类别则呈现增长-下降模式。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,这些发现凸显了由于感染相关疾病向心脏代谢疾病和晚期肝脏疾病的转变,临床和公共卫生负担日益增加,尤其是老年患者。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调需要进行综合的、针对年龄的管理和改进的 监测,以减少 死亡率 并优化 HBV 护理。这些结果有助于了解乙型肝炎及其相关合并症不断变化的临床特征。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制建立因果关系的能力。证据是中等的,因为它来自全国数据集,没有详细的实验室或临床程序。

abstract_zh: 背景 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 住院患者的临床特征越来越受到共存疾病和死亡模式的影响。本研究旨在评估 2012 年至 2023 年间首次因 HBV 住院患者的合并症和死亡率。材料和方法 利用全国总医院发病率研究的数据,对波兰首次 HBV 住院患者进行了 12 年全国回顾性分析。结果消化系统疾病(15.6%)、心血管疾病(10.5%)以及内分泌和代谢紊乱(9.6%)是最常见的合并症。2012 年至 2023 年间,消化系统疾病 (12.3%-27.4%) 和代谢疾病 (8.5%-18.5%) 疾病显着增加,而循环系统疾病则从 7.4% 上升至 18.6%,2019 年后趋于稳定。免疫相关疾病和泌尿生殖系统疾病在 2019 年后呈现持续增长,而包括肿瘤和呼吸系统疾病在内的几个类别则呈现增长-下降模式。高血压和肝纤维化是最常见的个体诊断,并且随着时间的推移持续或逐步增加。年龄分层分析显示,年轻患者的感染相关疾病向老年患者的心脏代谢和晚期肝脏疾病转变。死亡率从每 1000 人住院 6.8-15.9 人(2012-2019 年)增加到每 1000 人住院 23.1-30.7 人(2020-2023 年),在 2020-2021 年达到峰值,其中男性 死亡率 较高。结论 乙型肝炎首次住院越来越多地表现为多重发病率和死亡率上升,特别是在老年患者中。这些发现凸显了日益增长的临床和公共卫生负担,强调需要针对年龄进行综合管理和改进 监测,以减少 死亡率 并优化 HBV 护理。

title: Serum HBsAg cannot distinguish cccDNA activity from integrated HBV DNA expression in chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: HBsAg is currently used as the key serum biomarker to define functional cure of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Declining HBsAg is often interpreted as evidence of cccDNA elimination or durable transcriptional silencing. However, HBsAg can also be produced from transcriptionally active HBV DNA integrated into the host genome (iDNA), which can make serum HBsAg an unreliable indicator of the cccDNA activity or amount. METHODS: We combined intrahepatic HBsAg immunostaining, quantitative serum HBsAg levels (qHBsAg), and digital droplet PCR-based profiling of HBV DNA and RNA in liver biopsies to identify patients in whom HBsAg expression was predominantly driven by cccDNA or by iDNA. We then compared HBsAg abundance, isoform composition, secretion, and intrahepatic staining patterns between these groups. RESULTS: All three envelope proteins (L, M, S) were detectable in liver tissue and serum in both groups. The relative abundance of L and S, assessed by western blot and immunofluorescence, did not differ between iDNA- and cccDNA-driven cases. Across the combined cohort, intrahepatic HBsAg burden correlated with serum qHBsAg, indicating similar intracellular retention and secretion behavior. Importantly, all established intrahepatic HBsAg staining patterns (membranous and cytoplasmic subtypes) occurred in both groups, with no pattern uniquely associated with either source. CONCLUSIONS: Thus, iDNA can sustain HBsAg expression profiles that are indistinguishable from those generated by active cccDNA. Serum HBsAg alone may therefore fail to identify patients who have achieved cccDNA elimination or durable silencing. These findings suggest that the use of serum qHBsAg as a component of the functional cure endpoint in clinical studies warrants re-evaluation. IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) is the central biomarker used to define and monitor "functional cure" in chronic hepatitis B. This study shows that in patients with substantial HBV DNA integration, HBsAg is produced predominantly from integrated sequences, and that integration-derived HBsAg is indistinguishable from cccDNA-derived HBsAg in isoform composition, secretion behaviour, and histological distribution. Long-read sequencing confirmed that the integrated sequences generate full-length envelope transcripts. These findings are most relevant to virologists, hepatologists, clinical trialists, and regulators developing and evaluating HBV cure strategies. They indicate that serum HBsAg measurement cannot report cccDNA burden or transcriptional activity, and that focusing on HBsAg loss could miss "partial cure" states with favourable clinical outcomes. This warrants re-evaluation of HBsAg loss as a main functional cure endpoint, and supports the use of complementary or source-specific markers to assess treatment response.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the design does not include detailed statistical analyses or long-term follow-up. These findings suggest that the use of serum qHBsAg as a component of the functional cure endpoint in clinical studies warrants re-evaluation. IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) is the central biomarker used to define and monitor "functional cure" in chronic hepatitis B. This study shows that in patients with substantial HBV DNA integration, HBsAg is produced predominantly from integrated sequences, and that integration-derived HBsAg is indistinguishable from cccDNA-derived HBsAg in isoform composition, secretion behaviour, and histological distribution. Long-read sequencing confirmed that the integrated sequences generate full-length envelope transcripts. These findings are most relevant to virologists, hepatologists, clinical trialists, and regulators developing and evaluating HBV cure strategies. They indicate that serum HBsAg measurement cannot report cccDNA burden or transcriptional activity, and that focusing on HBsAg loss could miss "partial cure" states with favourable clinical outcomes. This warrants re-evaluation of HBsAg loss as a main functional cure endpoint, and supports the use of complementary or source-specific markers to assess treatment response.

title: Hepatitis B virus seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis burden among people living with HIV in Uganda: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HIV coinfection remains an important cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Uganda carries a substantial burden of both infections, yet evidence on HBV seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis among people living with HIV (PLHIV) has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review aimed to summarize available evidence from Uganda on HBV seroprevalence, correlates of HBV infection, and liver fibrosis burden among PLHIV. Methods This systematic review was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online (AJOL), WHO Global Index Medicus, Google Scholar, and medRxiv/bioRxiv from inception to December 2025 for studies conducted in Uganda among PLHIV reporting HBsAg seroprevalence, factors associated with HBV infection, or liver fibrosis outcomes. Eligible studies included observational designs. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Findings were synthesized narratively. Results A total of 14 studies were included. Most studies were cross-sectional and were conducted in Northern Uganda, Central Uganda, South-Western Uganda, and Lake Victoria fishing communities. Reported HBsAg seroprevalence among PLHIV varied across settings, with higher estimates generally observed in Northern Uganda and fishing communities than in some urban clinic-based populations. Frequently reported factors associated with HBV infection included male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence. Studies assessing liver fibrosis suggested a greater burden of significant fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals compared with HIV-monoinfected populations, although fibrosis definitions and diagnostic methods varied substantially across studies. Conclusions Available evidence indicates that HBV infection remains a significant comorbidity among PLHIV in Uganda, with substantial variation in seroprevalence across geographic settings. Male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and residence in higher-burden settings were among the most frequently reported associated factors. Studies also suggest a greater burden of liver fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals than among HIV-monoinfected populations. However, interpretation of findings is limited by methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of cross-sectional studies. Systematic review registration PROSPERO CRD420261349477.

title_original: Hepatitis B virus seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis burden among people living with HIV in Uganda: a systematic review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Uganda, focusing on seroprevalence, associated demographic and clinical factors, and liver fibrosis burden. The central question addresses the extent of HBV coinfection, its correlates, and its impact on liver disease in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online, WHO Global Index Medicus, Google Scholar, and medRxiv/bioRxiv from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies were observational designs conducted in Uganda among PLHIV, reporting HBsAg seroprevalence, associated factors, or liver fibrosis outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using JBI critical appraisal tools. Fourteen studies were included, with narrative synthesis of findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HBV infection remains a significant comorbidity among PLHIV in Uganda, with seroprevalence varying substantially across geographic settings. Higher HBsAg seroprevalence was generally observed in Northern Uganda and fishing communities compared to some urban clinic-based populations. Frequently reported factors associated with HBV infection included male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence. Studies assessing liver fibrosis suggested a greater burden of significant fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals compared with HIV-monoinfected populations, though definitions and diagnostic methods varied.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Interpretation of findings is limited by methodological heterogeneity, including the predominance of cross-sectional studies and variability in fibrosis definitions and diagnostic methods. The evidence base lacks standardized approaches to assess liver fibrosis and associated factors, which constrains comparability and robustness of conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Standardized diagnostic criteria and longitudinal study designs are needed to accurately quantify HBV seroprevalence, identify risk factors, and assess liver fibrosis burden among PLHIV in Uganda. Surveillance programs should prioritize high-risk settings such as Northern Uganda and fishing communities to target interventions effectively.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on hepatitis B virus (HBV) coinfection among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Uganda, focusing on seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis burden. Findings indicate substantial geographic variation in HBV seroprevalence, with higher rates in Northern Uganda and fishing communities. Male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence were frequently reported correlates of HBV infection. Liver fibrosis burden appeared greater in HBV-HIV coinfected individuals than in HIV-monoinfected populations, though diagnostic heterogeneity limited comparability. title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 血清流行率、乌干达艾滋病毒感染者的相关因素和肝纤维化负担:系统评价
source_body_en: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HIV coinfection remains an important cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Uganda carries a substantial burden of both infections, yet evidence on HBV seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis among people living with HIV (PLHIV) has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review aimed to summarize available evidence from Uganda on HBV seroprevalence, correlates of HBV infection, and liver fibrosis burden among PLHIV. Methods This systematic review was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online (AJOL), WHO Global Index Medicus, Google Scholar, and medRxiv/bioRxiv from inception to December 2025 for studies conducted in Uganda among PLHIV reporting HBsAg seroprevalence, factors associated with HBV infection, or liver fibrosis outcomes. Eligible studies included observational designs. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Findings were synthesized narratively. Results A total of 14 studies were included. Most studies were cross-sectional and were conducted in Northern Uganda, Central Uganda, South-Western Uganda, and Lake Victoria fishing communities. Reported HBsAg seroprevalence among PLHIV varied across settings, with higher estimates generally observed in Northern Uganda and fishing communities than in some urban clinic-based populations. Frequently reported factors associated with HBV infection included male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence. Studies assessing liver fibrosis suggested a greater burden of significant fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals compared with HIV-monoinfected populations, although fibrosis definitions and diagnostic methods varied substantially across studies. Conclusions Available evidence indicates that HBV infection remains a significant comorbidity among PLHIV in Uganda, with substantial variation in seroprevalence across geographic settings. Male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and residence in higher-burden settings were among the most frequently reported associated factors. Studies also suggest a greater burden of liver fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals than among HIV-monoinfected populations. However, interpretation of findings is limited by methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of cross-sectional studies. Systematic review registration PROSPERO CRD420261349477.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Hepatitis B Awareness, Knowledge Gaps, Health-Seeking Behaviour, Risk Perceptions, and Vaccination Status Among University Students in Bangladesh: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a significant public health problem globally. In Bangladesh, viral hepatitis is the most common liver disease, with approximately 10 million people infected with HBV. Methods The study was a cross‐sectional survey in which 440 respondents were randomly selected using Cochran's formula. The duration of the study was about 6 month (24th August 2024 to 28th February 2025). Data was gathered using a predesigned and structured questionnaire, which was distributed among the students. The collected data were then analysed utilizing Microsoft Excel 2016 and Stata 17 software for statistical processing and interpretation. Results Overall, the study found that respondents had a high level of awareness of hepatitis B, with most participants recognizing the disease and its major transmission routes and health consequences. Vaccine‐related knowledge was moderate, whereas hepatitis B vaccination uptake remained relatively low among the respondents and their family members. The mean (±SD) awareness, vaccine knowledge, and perception scores were 37.18 ± 11.16, 25.00 ± 10.88, and 22.38 ± 4.71 (each measured on a 50‐point scale), respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that male participants were more likely to be vaccinated against hepatitis B than female participants (aOR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.14–2.67). Participants with low awareness also had higher odds of being vaccinated than those with high awareness (aOR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.09–4.36), while no significant association was observed for moderate awareness. Conclusion Less than half of the respondents had received the hepatitis B vaccine, with the most common reason for non‐vaccination being a lack of awareness of their vaccination status. Slightly over half of the respondents demonstrated satisfactory knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B. These findings underscore the need for targeted education on hepatitis B infection, its risk factors, and the importance of vaccination among students in Bangladesh.

In Bangladesh, viral hepatitis is the most common liver disease, with approximately 10 million people infected with HBV. Methods The study was a cross‐sectional survey in which 440 respondents were randomly selected using Cochran's formula. The duration of the study was about 6 month (24th August 2024 to 28th February 2025). Data was gathered using a predesigned and structured questionnaire, which was distributed among the students. The collected data were then analysed utilizing Microsoft Excel 2016 and Stata 17 software for statistical processing and interpretation. Results Overall, the study found that respondents had a high level of awareness of hepatitis B, with most participants recognizing the disease and its major transmission routes and health consequences. Vaccine‐related knowledge was moderate, whereas hepatitis B vaccination uptake remained relatively low among the respondents and their family members. The mean (±SD) awareness, vaccine knowledge, and perception scores were 37.18 ± 11.16, 25.00 ± 10.88, and 22.38 ± 4.71 (each measured on a 50‐point scale), respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that male participants were more likely to be vaccinated against hepatitis B than female participants (aOR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.14–2.67). Participants with low awareness also had higher odds of being vaccinated than those with high awareness (aOR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.09–4.36), while no significant association was observed for moderate awareness. Conclusion Less than half of the respondents had received the hepatitis B vaccine, with the most common reason for non‐vaccination being a lack of awareness of their vaccination status. Slightly over half of the respondents demonstrated satisfactory knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B. These findings underscore the need for targeted education on hepatitis B infection, its risk factors, and the importance of vaccination among students in Bangladesh.

title: Geospatial Discrepancy of Chronic Hepatitis B and Hepatitis D Testing in Alberta: A Population-Based Spatial Analysis.
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The geographic distribution of CHB and alignment of anti-HDV testing with CHB burden remain poorly defined. We aimed to examine if anti-HDV testing and seropositivity align with areas of highest CHB burden. Adults with CHB (2014-2022) were identified using a validated serologic algorithm in the provincial laboratory database capturing HBV/HDV serology. Cases were geolocated to Aggregate Dissemination Areas (ADAs), linked to Alberta Health Services zones and rural-urban continuum levels. Age- and sex-standardized CHB prevalence was calculated per ADA using the 2016 Canadian Census. Descriptive mapping, global spatial autocorrelation and local hotspot analysis were used to assess spatial clustering. Among 8317 persons with CHB, the provincial age- and sex-standardized prevalence was 1.70 per 1000 population (95% CI, 1.66-1.74). Prevalence ranged from 2.15 per 1000 in metropolitan areas to 0.40 per 1000 in remote regions and was higher in Calgary than Edmonton (2.53 vs. Overall, 17.5% of CHB patients were tested for anti-HDV, and 4.1% of those tested were anti-HDV positive. CHB prevalence hotspots were concentrated in metropolitan ADAs, whereas hotspots of anti-HDV testing and positivity showed only partial overlap with these high-burden areas. CHB burden in Alberta is geographically clustered, particularly within specific neighbourhoods of metropolitan cities, whereas anti-HDV testing remains infrequent and only partially aligned with high-burden areas. Reflex or systematic anti-HDV testing, paired with geographically informed outreach, may improve case detection.

CHB burden in Alberta is geographically clustered, particularly within specific neighbourhoods of metropolitan cities, whereas anti-HDV testing remains infrequent and only partially aligned with high-burden areas. Reflex or systematic anti-HDV testing, paired with geographically informed outreach, may improve case detection.

title: Single-Cell Hepatitis B Sequencing Reveals Distinct Viral Infection Events Consistent With Superinfection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The high error rate of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) polymerase leads to a genetically diverse quasispecies in individuals with chronic hepatitis B. Data regarding the propagation of these variants in individual hepatocytes may provide insight into viral replication and diversity of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), which is the template for HBV replication. METHODS: We developed sequencing protocols to characterize HBV diversity between and within hepatocytes using RNA extracted from individually isolated hepatocytes. We sequenced HBV in >200 hepatocytes in 4 liver biopsies from people with HIV/HBV (HB1, HB2, HB3, HB6). RESULTS: We found that 2 biopsies (HB1 and HB6) showed HBV diversity between hepatocytes that met an experimentally identified threshold. Specifically, in HB1, HBV sequences from 86 individual cells were from 2 different haplotypes of genotype D: 70.2% of cells with haplotype a, 5.8% with haplotype b, and 24% with both haplotypes in the same cell. Furthermore, within single hepatocytes, up to 3 different HBV sequences were present per cell, including some cells with both genotypes A and D. HB6, who received years of lamivudine monotherapy, had evidence of drug resistance mutations distributed among hepatocytes and demonstrated up to 3 different sequences, including wild-type and drug-resistant sequences, in the same hepatocyte. Modeling of infected hepatocytes did not reveal evidence of local HBV spread based on spatial proximity. CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, our findings demonstrate that individual hepatocytes may harbor multiple, transcriptionally active HBV cccDNA molecules, which likely arose from distinct infection events.
