source_records.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global public health challenge. Tripartite motif-containing protein 22 (TRIM22) is an interferon-stimulated gene, but whether its E3 ubiquitin ligase activity is involved in regulating HBV replication remains unclear. Accumulating evidence indicates that lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) promotes HBV replication, and LDHA inhibition represents a promising host-directed antiviral strategy for HBV therapy. Serum samples from 208 CHB patients were collected to analyze the correlation between lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels and clinical parameters. The GSE65359 dataset was used, and TRIM22-overexpressing cell models were established. The association between TRIM22 and glycolysis was assessed by transcriptomic sequencing, targeted metabolomics and Seahorse extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) analysis. TRIM22-interacting proteins were screened by co-immunoprecipitation coupled with LC-MS/MS and validated. TRIM22 domain-deletion mutants were constructed and together with MG132 treatment, were used to verify the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation of LDHA, as well as the effects of the mutations on the RIG-I-MAVS pathway and HBV markers. Functional rescue experiments were performed via LDHA co-transfection and Amlexanox treatment. Additionally, LDHA overexpression was used to assess its downstream effects. Clinical analysis revealed that serum LDH levels positively correlated with both HBV viral load and liver injury markers. Public database analysis showed that TRIM22 was negatively correlated with LDHA and lactate transporters in CHB liver tissues. TRIM22 overexpression attenuated glycolysis and activated the TCA cycle. ECAR analysis confirmed that TRIM22 overexpression suppressed glycolytic flux. LDHA was identified as a novel interacting protein of TRIM22. Further experiments confirmed that TRIM22 binds LDHA through its coiled-coil domain and promotes its K48-linked ubiquitination via its RING domain. This degradation inhibited HBV replication and enhanced activation of the Retinoic-acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) - Mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS) pathway. Transcriptomic and functional studies further demonstrated that LDHA overexpression promoted HBV replication by suppressing the RIG-I-MAVS pathway, potentially through downregulation of C-C motif chemokine ligand 3 like 1 (CCL3L1) and C-C motif chemokine ligand 24 (CCL24). Our findings define a novel mechanism by which TRIM22 ubiquitinates LDHA through its RING domain, thereby inhibiting the glycolytic pathway and activating the RIG-I-MAVS pathway, consequently suppressing HBV replication. This provides a potential foundation for developing new therapeutic strategies against HBV.

title: UHPLC-Orbitrap-HRMS-based metabolite identification and profiling of methylophiopogonone A, A bioactive constituent from Ophiopogon japonicus.
abstract: Methylophiopogonone A (MON-A), an anti-inflammatory constituent of Ophiopogon japonicus, demonstrates therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B and SARS-CoV-2 infection. This study aimed to investigate its metabolic profile using liver microsomes and cryopreserved hepatocytes from humans and three preclinical species (rat, dog, and monkey). MON-A was incubated separately with each system, and the samples were analyzed by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole/Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Orbitrap-HRMS) in positive electrospray ionization mode. Data were processed using Compound Discoverer software with mass defect filtering. Metabolite structures were characterized based on accurate mass and MS2 fragment ions. A total of 14 metabolites were identified. The primary metabolic pathways included hydroxylation, oxidative methylenedioxyphenyl (MDP) ring-opening, oxidation, and glucuronidation. M11 (a glucuronide conjugate) was the most abundant metabolite across all species. Additionally, four glutathione (GSH) conjugates were detected, indicating the formation of reactive metabolites, notably ortho-quinone and quinone methide species. The formation of quinone methide species revealed that C2-C3 double bond is essential for the metabolic activation of the A-ring. This systematic study clarifies the metabolic fate of MON-A, providing important insights into its biotransformation pathways and potential for reactive metabolite formation. The results establish a foundation for evaluating both the therapeutic efficacy and safety profile of this anti-inflammatory candidate during preclinical development.
journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Analysis

title: Contribution of medical imaging in the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma at the CNHU-HKM in Cotonou
abstract: Introduction: The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Global Cancer Observatory rank hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as the sixth most common cancer in the world and the fourth leading cause of cancer death. According to GLOBOCAN 2022, sub-Saharan Africa is a very highly endemic area. In Benin, despite the high frequency of cirrhosis and viral liver disease, local data remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the contribution and compare the performance of medical imaging techniques (ultrasound and CT) in the diagnosis of HCC at the CNHU-HKM in Cotonou. Methods: This was a retrospective, descriptive and analytical study conducted over a one-year period (from 23 May 2023 to 23 May 2024) using the Cotonou Cancer Registry. The study comprehensively included 118 patients suspected of HCC. Results: The mean age of the patients was 47.46 years with a clear male predominance (sex ratio: 3.72). The main etiologies identified were viral hepatitis B (61.02%) and chronic alcoholism (37.28%). On ultrasound, hypervascular nodules on cirrhotic liver were hypervascularized on cirrhotic liver. On multiphase CT scan, HCC was characterized by arterial wash-in (94.91%) followed by portal wash-out (90.67%). CT had a higher sensitivity (98.1%) than ultrasound (85.2%), while ultrasound maintained perfect specificity (100%). Conclusion: The complementarity of ultrasound and CT remains essential to optimize the non-invasive diagnostic management of HCC in our health context.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Anxiety, depression, and health-related quality of life in adults with hemophilic arthropathy: A cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUNDHemophilic arthritis can lead to chronic joint pain, functional limitations, and decreased quality of life, and may be accompanied by psychological problems such as anxiety and depression.Current research on the psychological status of adult patients with hemophilic arthritis and its impact on health-related quality of life remains limited. AIMTo investigate prevalence of anxiety and depression among adults with hemophilic arthropathy and analyze impact on health-related quality of life. METHODSA convenience sample of 360 adult patients with hemophilic arthropathy who attended the First Affiliated Hospital of Shandong First Medical University (Qianfoshan Hospital, Shandong Province, China) between January 2024 and December 2025 was recruited for this cross-sectional study.The Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), visual analog scale, and 36-item Short Form Health Survey were used to assess anxiety and depression levels; joint pain levels; and quality of life, respectively. RESULTS A total of 155 patients (43.1%) tested positive for HADS-Anxiety (HADS-A) and HADS-Depression (HADS-D) (HADS-A or HADS-D ≥ 8). Multivariate regression analysisrevealed that HADS-D scores (β = -0.415,P < 0.001), the number of affected joints (β = -0.208,P < 0.001), visual analog scale score (β = -0.174,P < 0.001), untreated or irregular treatment (β = -0.165,P < 0.001), and concomitant hepatitis C virus infection (β = -0.098,P = 0.012) were independent predictors of the Physical Health Subscale.HADS-D scores (β = -0.502,P < 0.001), HADS-A scores (β = -0.223,P < 0.001), and the number of affected joints (β = -0.129,P = 0.005) were independent predictors of the Mental Health Subscale.4 / 27 CONCLUSION Hemophilic arthropathy elevates anxiety and depression in adults, impairing quality of life.Joint pain, multi-joint involvement, and non-standardized treatment are key risks, necessitating for routine psychological assessment and comprehensive intervention.
